full_judgment:
Naima Haider J: The above Rule was issued by this Court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why Order No. 1 dated 4-4-2016 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 so far it relates to the issuing of show cause notice and direction upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to maintain status quo with regard to possession of flats as described in (Gho) and (Umo) schedule to the petition and disconnecting gas, water, electricity supply, security and lift in the said flats till further order shall not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that: The petitioner filed the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 stating, inter alia, that the schedule 'Ka' of the petition comprises of 4 (four) buildings, namely, Meghna Bhaban, Kushiara Bhaban, Padma Bhaban and Surma Bhaban which are being constructed on 2.50 acres of land situated at Bisil Mouza under Shah Ali Police station at Dhaka. Meghna Bhaban, a 15-storied building with defined boundary, is the `Kha' schedule property of the case. Apartment No. 5/K measuring 1483 square feet situated at the level-5 of the Meghna Bhaban .along with 0.1 decimal undemarcated and undivided land is the 'Ga' schedule property of the case. Schedule `Cho' is comprised of the common facilities which includes the Community Hall, Play ground, Mosque, Maktab etc. 

 8. The petitioner by legal notice dated 15-12-2015 requested the opposite parties to complete the incomplete works. Thereafter, the petitioner served another notice dated 19-1-2016 for appointment of arbitrator. The opposite parties failed to appoint arbitrator and, as such, the petitioner was compelled to file Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 115 of 2016 before the District Judge, Dhaka on 23-2-2016 under the name of unregistered society namely "MRC Meghna Bhaban Flat Owners Society". 

 9. The opposite parties on 15-10-2015 constituted a society namely, "MRC Meghna Bhaban Flat Owners Society" with the instant petitioner as President of the said society and 10 (ten) other flat purchasers as members of the Executive Committee. The opposite parties permitted to use the flat No. 9/C at level-9 as temporary office of the Society. Since then, the petitioner and other purchasers are operating the affairs of the Samity using schedule- "Uma" flat No. 9/C as the office. The petitioner filed the Arbitration Miscellaneous case on the basis of clause No. 50 of the agreement dated 3-12-2006 executed between the petitioner and the opposite parties for appointment of arbitrator. The petitioner in prayer "Kha" of the said miscellaneous case also prayed for temporary injunction under section 7(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001. 

 10. The petitioner on 4-4-2016 also filed an application under section 7(Ka) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 in the aforesaid arbitration Miscellaneous Case, stating, amongst that the opposite parties without completing the incomplete works i.e. Community Hall at the 3rd floor, society office, mosque, return of excess money, registration of 60/70 flats etc and published a notice on 30-1-2016 showing transfer of the building to the petitioners. Petitioner objected to the notice and informed the opposite parties that they can not transfer the building to the owners society without firstly completing the incomplete works. The petitioner came to know from reliable source that the opposite party is trying to hand over management of the services to the owners society. The opposite party is earning monthly rent amounting to Taka 10,00,000 (Taka Ten Lacs) by giving lease of the 3rd floor (which is the purchased space of the Meghna Bhaban Flat Owners) to the Manarat International University and PIF Securities Limited. The opposite party is bound to return Taka 5,00,00,000 (Taka Five Crore) and give registration of the 60/70 flats. The opposite party can maintain the services at the existing rate of Taka 2,500 (Taka Two Thousand Five hundred). The petitioner prayed for injunction restraining the opposite parties from using the 3rd floor for any purpose other than common use, receiving rent from Manarat International University and PFI Securities Limited, disconnecting the water, electricity, gas connection, remove the guard, cleaning staff and liftmen and not to increase the monthly service charge from Taka 2,500 and not to dispossess the petitioner from apartment No. 9/C at level-9 of the building. 

 11. The learned District Judge, Dhaka by his order No. 1 dated 4-4-2016 admitted the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016. By the same order District Judge, Dhaka most illegally issued show cause notice upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 and illegally directed the opposite parties to maintain status quo with regard to possession of flats as described in (Gha) and (Umo) schedule to the petition and disconnecting gas, water, electricity supply, security and lift in above flats till further order. District Judge, Dhaka fixed the next date on 12-5-2016 for SR and AD. The petitioner has been directed to file postal receipts by 12-5-2016. 

 16. The Deed of Agreement for allotment of premises dated 3-12-2006 executed between the petitioner No. 1 company and the opposite party No. 1 Professor Zainul Abedin and his wife Delwara Begum apartment No. 5K at level-5 was allotted to the purchasers, a Supplementary Deed of Agreement dated 16-3-2009 and a Deed of Revised Supplementary Agreement dated 24-2-2011 between the parties. The opposite party No. 1 and his wife received possession of their flat No. 5/K in full ready condition on 26-2-2011 without any objection by signing the Certificate of handing and taking over physical possession. The registration of their apartment was completed on 20-6-2012. The opposite party No. 1 is not the sole purchaser of the said flat, he along with his wife are the purchasers of the said flat. So, the petitioner alone has no authority to file the case as sole petitioner. In the same manner, all the flat purchasers of Meghna Bhaban have received possession of their purchased flats from the year 2010. 

 18. The notice under section 36 of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010 is a pre-condition before taking any legal action against the development but in the instant Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, no such notice has been served upon the petitioners by the opposite party No. 1 at any point of time before filing of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, as such the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case is not maintainable. More so, the District Judge has got no authority to compel the parties to sit on arbitration as per section 36(5) of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010. It is the exclusive jurisdiction of the respective court mentioned in the Act. 

 19. The MRC Meghna Bhaban Flat Owner Society as petitioner No. 1 filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 115 of 2016 under section 12 of the Arbitration Ad, 2001 but after hearing the petitioners of the said case realized that their application is not maintainable and they prayed for dismissal of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 115 of 2016 on 4-4-2016 and the said case was rejected. Thereafter, on the same date 4-4-2016, the present Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 has been filed by the petitioner without serving any fresh notice as required by section 12 of the Arbitration Act. 2001 as such the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 is not maintainable in the present form and forum. So the order of direction passed exparte against the opposite party Nos. 1-5 of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 is not sustainable in law. 

 20. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the Order No. 1 dated 4-4-2016 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 so far it relates to the issuing of show cause notice and direction upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to maintain status quo with regard to possession of flats as described in (Gha) and (Umo) schedule to the plaint and disconnecting gas,' water, electricity supply, security and lift in the said flats till further order, the petitioners have moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule. 

 21. The opposite party No. 1 entered appearance by counter affidavit against the Civil Revisional application. The case of the opposite party No. 1 is that: As to completion of construction of Meghna Bhaban is correct but other statements as to construction of common office and community space will be constructed after completion of all our building of the project is not correct. Community and common space would be constructed with the respective building which is not concerned with completion of four buildings. The Brochure is published by the developer, and the RAJUK approved plan with floor arrangement. The developer company sent a short brochure to opposite party No. 1 mentioning playground for the child gymnasium, prayer room etc. facilities in the respective building. 

 23. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, leaned Senior Advocate along with Mr Mir Md Joynal Abedin, the learned Advocate for the petitioner at the outset submits that the petitioner filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 for appointment of arbitrator and on the same date filed a petition under 7(Ka) of the said Act praying ad-interim order of injunction that the opposite parties cannot leave the Schedule "Kha" Meghna Bhaban without finishing the construction works, unlawfully evict the petitioner and other flat owners from the schedule "Gha" and "limo" and restraining the opposite parties to disconnect the Gas, Water, Electricity line and also withdrawing the security guard and cleaning staff arbitrarily and unlawfully. 

 24. Mr Alam next submits that the opposite party No. 1 did not serve any arbitration notice giving 30 days time to the petitioners which is clear violation of the mandatory provision of law as such the instant Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 filed under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 filed by the opposite party No. 1 is not at all maintainable. He further submits that the sub-section 3 of section 7Ka of the Arbitration Act, 2001 service of notice upon the opposite party is pre-requisite condition but the Court below passed the exparte order of injunction without serving any notice to the petitioners as such the court below committed an error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 25. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, along with Mr Md Abdul Baten Sheikh, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 submits that considering the balance of convenience and inconvenience, the learned Trial Court below passed the order of status quo in respect of possession of flats as described in (Gha) and (Umo) schedule to the suit property and disconnecting gas, water, electricity supply, security and 'lift to the suit property. But the present petitioners filed Civil Revision in this Court without stating anything about the said order of status quo and by misleading and stating the merit of the Arbitration Misc. Case No. 206 of 2016, obtained the Rule and, as such, the same is required to be discharged. 

 27. On perusal of the record it appears that the petitioner filed the above noted Civil Revisional application against the Judgment and Order No. 1 dated 4-4-2016 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 so far it relates to the issuing of show cause notice and direction upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to maintain status-quo with regard to possession of flats as described in (Gha) and (Umo) schedule to the petition and disconnecting gas, water, electricity supply, security and lift in the said flats till further order. 

 28. Admittedly, the petitioner filed the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 stating, inter alia, that the schedule 'Ka' of the petition comprises of 4 (four) buildings, namely, Meghna Bhaban, Kushiara Bhaban, Padma Bhaban and Surma Bhaban which are being constructed on 2.50 acres of land situated at Bisil Mouza under Shah Ali Police station at Dhaka. Meghna Bhaban, a 15-storied building with defined boundary is the 'Kha' schedule property of the case. Apartment No. 5/K measuring 1,483 square feet situated at the level-5 of the Meghna Bhaban along with 0.100 decimal undemarcated and undivided land is the 'Ga' schedule property of the case. Schedule 'Gha' is comprised of the common facilities which includes the Community Hall, Play ground. Mosque, Maktab etc. 

 31. We find the court below' failed to consider that the petitioner of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 received possession of his ‘flat No. 5/K in full ready condition on 26-2-2011 without any objection and registration of his apartment was completed on 20-6-2012 as such the facts does not necessitate the passing of any ad-interim order against the opposite party without serving notice upon them. So, the Court below committed an error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 32. We note that the Court below miserably failed to consider that the petitioner of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 did not serve any notice upon the opposite party of the case seeking arbitration and, as such, he has no cause of action to file the said Arbitration Miscellaneous Case. The Court below upon misconception of law miserably failed to consider that as per the provisions laid down in section 36 of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010 District Judge has got no jurisdiction to entertain any application under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 for appointment of Arbitrators and also has no jurisdiction to entertain any application under section 7Ka of the Arbitration Act, 2001 to pass an order of injunction in a case of dispute between the Developer and Flat purchaser. 

 33. We also find that under section 36 of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010 there is a pre-condition of serving notice before taking any legal action against the Developer but in the instant Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, no such notice has been served upon the petitioners by the opposite party No. 1 at any point of time before filing of the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case, as such the Arbitration Miscellaneous is not maintainable and the District Judge has got no authority to compel the parties to sit for an arbitration as per section 36(5) of the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010. 

 37. The Order No. 1 dated 4-4-2016 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 2016 so far it relates to the issuing of show cause notice and direction upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to maintain status quo with regard to possession of flats as described in (Gho) and (Umo) schedule to the petition and disconnecting gas, water, electricity supply, security and lift in the said flats till further order is hereby set aside.
